trust_decision.summary: A per-user MCP tool grant is decided server-side by allowed_mcp_tools() from the v2 grant's mcp_tools whitelist and consumed when the chat pipeline builds its deferred-tool pool; at the pinned commit an unset whitelist (None) means allow-everything, so a non-admin user with the default grant reaches every configured MCP tool.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('missing MCP tool authorization') names the only per-user MCP authorization function; its own docstring calls it the enforcement point for deferred tools (tool_access.py:14-16), so an engineer reading only the summary starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: /api/v1/chat websocket turn; partner channel turn (same pipeline)
fix_sites.module_kind: chat pipeline consume point (combine of caller filter and user grant)

fix_sites.entry_point: partner inbound channel message (Telegram/Slack/Teams/... -> PartnerRuntime) ; partner config field at deeptutor/services/partners/manager.py:135-136
fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation (partner config authorisation, services/partners package)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A partner turn runs as the admin owner's own agent, so its MCP list is the owner's configuration (None = all MCP, manager.py:135-136) and not a user grant; a solver can argue the partner path is owner-authorised and out of scope for a 'non-admin user' advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Partners rely on mcp_tools=None meaning 'all MCP tools' (owner default, and [] meaning 'MCP off'); a blanket default-deny in allowed_mcp_tools() returns set() for any non-admin, and combine_whitelists() then intersects every partner filter down to empty, silently removing all MCP tools from every partner. Admins must also stay unrestricted.

O6_input_shapes: mcp_tools absent / null on the grant (the default produced by empty_grant and by the admin UI, web/features/multi-user/components/GrantEditor.tsx:18)
mcp_tools: [names] (explicit whitelist, compared against the wrapped tool name)
caller-scoped mcp_tools_filter: present list vs absent (partner turn), intersected via combine_whitelists
no grant file at all for a real non-admin user (load_grant falls back to empty_grant)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A model-emitted tool call is executed by name through the generic dispatcher: registry.execute() runs any registered MCP adapter, with no per-user grant lookup, so naming mcp_<server>_<tool> in the prompt invokes a tool the deferred loader never exposed.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The deferred loader documents itself as enforced 'not only at manifest time, so the model cannot load an off-list tool by guessing its name' (deferred_tools.py:85-89), so a solver can argue execution is already covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different packages: deeptutor.multi_user -> deeptutor.agents.chat -> deeptutor.runtime.registry -> deeptutor.core.agentic (3 files, 4 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Capability pipelines (explore_context, research, question) dispatch tool calls through the same registry without ever building a deferred loader or consulting the MCP grant, so an MCP tool name emitted in those turns executes unfiltered.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Those pipelines only advertise their own allowlisted schemas (e.g. deeptutor/agents/research/pipeline.py:1732-1736), so a solver can argue MCP tools are not reachable from them and the chat pipeline is the only surface that matters.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different packages (deeptutor.capabilities, deeptutor.agents.research/question) from the landing point in deeptutor.multi_user

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists but is unused; a maintainer adding a debug/status or plugin surface would plausibly call it instead of going through the deferred loader.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-user MCP tool listing that returns the live registry rather than the caller's allowed set.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already enumerates registry.deferred_tools() for the admin/partner UIs; adding a user-facing variant is a one-line reuse.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper is deliberately public for capabilities that want to invoke a single tool outside parallel dispatch (docstring at tool_dispatch.py:341-343).
